status: Five full-text sources inspected for the conditional positive-FI ADHM pushforward, its N-tuple fixed points and tangent weights, the N=2* shifted tangent numerator, the rank-one specialization, and the S4 regulator caveat. The main physics theorem is restricted to N≥2 because the inspected framed-ADHM definition has that domain; a self-contained rank-one charge-one supplier supports the U(1) example. The batch-61 noncompact Borel–Moore carriers and current Step 1 readiness records are ready; the ADHM readiness chain remains escalated and the S4 postulate readiness record is missing. No continuum path-integral identity is claimed.

sources.title: Nikita A. Nekrasov, Seiberg–Witten Prepotential from Instanton Counting
sources.locator: §1, equation (1.3); §§3.1–3.6, PDF pp. 12–19: equivariant pushforward, ADHM, noncompactness, positive-FI resolution, tangent complex, partition fixed points, and contour residue discussion.

source_review.read_extent: The displayed series and its localized equivariant pushforward meaning were inspected in the full PDF at §1, equation (1.3), including the following coefficient-ring explanation.
source_review.supports: The source-specific formal instanton series is organized coefficientwise by charge using an equivariant pushforward of the unit.
source_review.limitations: The source's field-theory construction does not prove that a noncompact pushforward exists for every ADHM regulator or that a continuum path integral equals it.

source_review.read_extent: The complete discussion of the nonzero real moment-map level, exceptional divisors, and small-size/runaway noncompactness was inspected at PDF pp. 14–15, equation (3.9), together with the adjacent paragraphs.
source_review.supports: A positive-FI/noncommutative resolved model is a distinct regulator for the instanton quotient, and the unregulated ADHM space is noncompact.
source_review.limitations: The source changes or regularizes the gauge-theory model; it does not construct an ordinary proper pushforward on the noncompact quotient.

source_review.read_extent: The ADHM deformation data, torus fixed-point equations, tangent-weight residues, and partition-indexed poles were inspected in full-text chunks at PDF pp. 16–19, equations (3.13)–(3.20).
source_review.supports: The source-specific Ω-background calculation associates partition-indexed fixed points and tangent weights to instanton contributions.
source_review.limitations: Its contour prescription and formal gauge-theory measure are not used as a proof of the noncompact Borel–Moore pushforward; the local theorem depends on a separate mathematical localization supplier.

contents.name: The source's contour residue prescription
contents.reason: This batch states a generic rational-function identity only and does not assert a contour integral or adopt the contour deformation as a proof.

sources.title: Hiraku Nakajima and Kota Yoshioka, Lectures on Instanton Counting
sources.locator: §3.1, PDF pp. 17–19, fixed-point classification and Theorem 3.2 tangent character; Abstract and §4 for deformed partition functions as equivariant generating functions.

contents.name: §3.1 fixed points indexed by N-tuples of partitions

source_review.read_extent: The full fixed-locus description and total-box constraint were inspected in PDF pp. 17–18, including the decomposition into framed rank-one ideal sheaves supported at the rotation fixed point.
source_review.supports: For the framed torsion-free-sheaf model, torus-fixed data are indexed by N-tuples of finite Young diagrams of total size k.
source_review.limitations: This is a sheaf-moduli statement. The source cites rather than proves the relevant sheaf/ASD identification; this batch makes no such identification.

source_review.read_extent: The full displayed tangent-character formula and the adjacent definitions of arm and leg data were inspected in PDF pp. 18–19.
source_review.supports: The T²×T_G tangent representation at a partition fixed point, with the framing-character convention recorded in the source.
source_review.limitations: The assigned theorem uses the actual current ADHM character supplier and cites this treatment as an independent formula check; the tangent weights are not imported without a convention match.

contents.name: Abstract and §4 deformed equivariant partition series

source_review.read_extent: The abstract and the beginning/definition portions of §4 were inspected, including the stated generating-function role of equivariant integration over instanton moduli.
source_review.supports: The source-specific Nekrasov function is treated as a charge-generating equivariant partition series.
source_review.limitations: The notes do not supply the new batch's exact noncompact Borel–Moore pushforward construction for the positive-FI ADHM quotient.

contents.name: §3.1 locally-free sheaf/ASD correspondence
contents.reason: The text cites Donaldson for the locally-free sheaf identification rather than proving the ADHM-to-ASD correspondence required for an ordinary continuum instanton claim; no such claim is made here.

sources.title: Nikita Nekrasov and Andrei Okounkov, Seiberg–Witten Theory and Random Partitions

source_review.read_extent: The complete rotation-vector-field and two-plane parameter matrices were inspected in PDF pp. 8–9, equations (2.6)–(2.8), along with the twisted-formalism explanation.
source_review.supports: The Ω-background is associated with the two commuting rotations of the orthogonal coordinate planes and their parameters ε1, ε2.
source_review.limitations: The assigned item uses the finite-dimensional torus action as its explicit mathematical definition and makes no claim that an infinite-dimensional action integral is constructed.

source_review.read_extent: The opening definition of the constant Poisson tensor and Moyal-product deformation was inspected in PDF pp. 11–14.
source_review.supports: The source's regulator is a noncommutative deformation compatible with the Ω-background discussion.
source_review.limitations: The source's regulator is model-specific and does not prove an S4 noncommutative construction or regulator-independent continuum limit.

source_review.read_extent: The full opening of §3.1 and displayed sum/product formulas (3.5)–(3.10) were inspected in PDF pp. 18–20.
source_review.supports: A source-specific Ω-background partition function is expressed as an instanton-charge series over N-tuples of partitions with explicit weights.
source_review.limitations: The infinite determinant products require the source's own regularization, and this formula does not prove equality with a general continuum field-theory integral.

contents.name: §§4–5 prepotential and thermodynamic limits
contents.reason: No ε→0 limit, Seiberg–Witten prepotential identity, random-partition limit, or analytic convergence statement is claimed in this batch.

source_review.read_extent: The full §6.1 fixed-point product and its relation to the adjoint-hypermultiplet mass parameter were inspected in the full PDF.
source_review.supports: The source-specific N=2* instanton factor weights each tangent contribution by a mass-shifted numerator and is organized as a formal charge series.
source_review.limitations: The infinite products and physical interpretation retain their source-specific regularization; this source does not prove the batch mathematical Borel–Moore pushforward or a continuum path-integral identity.

sources.title: Vasily Pestun, Localization of Gauge Theory on a Four-Sphere and Supersymmetric Wilson Loops
sources.locator: §1 equations (1.3)–(1.4), PDF pp. 3–4, the regulator discussion after (1.4); §4.3 equations (4.47)–(4.50), PDF pp. 31–32; and §5 equations (5.11)–(5.12), PDF pp. 38–39.

contents.name: §1 S4 matrix-model structure and local instanton factor

source_review.read_extent: The full displayed structural formulae (1.3)–(1.5), the parameter ε1=ε2=R−1, and the explanation of Zinst were inspected in PDF pp. 3–4.
source_review.supports: In the source's S4 localization formula, the local Nekrasov instanton factor appears alongside classical and one-loop factors, with both pole sectors represented by the modulus square.
source_review.limitations: The assigned theorem computes only the formal local factor; it does not derive the matrix integral, one-loop determinant, or full S4 path integral.

source_review.read_extent: The complete paragraph following equation (1.4) was inspected: the source says the flat-space instanton factor is noncommutatively regularized and assumes, without constructing it, a compatible S4 deformation agreeing near the poles.
source_review.supports: The physical use of the flat Ω-background series as an S4 factor is conditional on the source's regulator premise.
source_review.limitations: This is not a proof of the noncommutative S4 theory or of equality to an unregulated continuum integral.

contents.name: Complete S4 matrix integral and one-loop determinant
contents.reason: The assigned theorem deliberately claims neither the complete S4 matrix integral nor a one-loop determinant formula.

source_review.read_extent: The complete continuation of the mass and Coulomb variables to imaginary values and the definition m=i m_E with m_E real were inspected around equation (4.47), PDF pp. 31–32.
source_review.supports: The source convention used in this batch takes the Euclidean hypermultiplet mass parameter to m=i m_E.
source_review.limitations: This is a convention for the source’s Euclidean contour, not an independently derived physical mass prescription.

source_review.read_extent: The full product in equation (5.11), the preceding explanation that the adjoint factor is the tangent-bundle factor with weights shifted by hypermultiplet mass, and the note defining m-tilde were inspected in PDF p. 38.
source_review.supports: For each fixed point the N=2* factor is the product of tangent weights shifted by -m-tilde over the tangent Euler product, with m-tilde=m+(epsilon1+epsilon2)/2.
source_review.limitations: This is the source’s formal instanton-factor prescription; it does not establish the noncompact Borel–Moore pushforward or construct the S4 noncommutative deformation.

source_review.read_extent: The complete U(2), k=1 expression and the simplification in equation (5.12) were inspected in PDF pp. 38–39.
source_review.supports: The two one-box fixed-point terms simplify to the mass-shifted U(2) coefficient used in the B-page example.
source_review.limitations: The example independently derives the simplification from its two tangent-weight products; the source formula is a convention cross-check, not a proof of the upstream fixed-point classification.

contents.name: §5 equation (5.11) specialized to the rank-one one-box weight

source_review.read_extent: The full general U(N) fixed-point product and equivariant mass shift in equation (5.11) were inspected; for N=1 and one box its two tangent factors are epsilon1 and epsilon2.
source_review.supports: The rank-one one-box coefficient uses the same inverse-tangent-Euler denominator and the two tangent weights shifted by the adjoint mass parameter.
source_review.limitations: This is the source’s physical formal factor. The explicit scalar quotient and normalized Borel–Moore trace are proved by the local lemma; no continuum path-integral identity is imported.

sources.title: Dan Edidin and William Graham, Localization in Equivariant Intersection Theory and the Bott Residue Formula
sources.locator: §4, Theorem 2 and its complete proof, printed pp. 7–8: explicit fixed-locus class decomposition for smooth varieties and the normal Euler denominator.

source_review.read_extent: The full §4 argument was inspected, including smoothness of the fixed locus, nonzero normal weights, invertibility of the Euler class, and the self-intersection derivation of Theorem 2.
source_review.supports: The local rank-one calculation uses the same finite-dimensional equivariant Chern-class restriction and normal Euler denominator structure at its unique fixed point.
source_review.limitations: Edidin–Graham prove the class formula in equivariant Chow theory; they do not provide the normalized equivariant Borel–Moore proper-trace construction used here. The local BM conclusion is proved from the current Borel–Moore supplier and does not rely on substituting the Chow pushforward.
